manifest.name: dsh-workbuddy-codex
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns a local WorkBuddy gateway into a model backend for every client: registers the workbuddy model provider (mounted from dsh-llm-workbuddy), supervises the wb2api gateway, and runs both bundled protocol bridges — Responses for Codex, Anthropic Messages for Claude Code and Claude Desktop
manifest.author: kangjiazhen

bundle.text:
# dsh-workbuddy-codex — keeps the local WorkBuddy reverse-proxy chain answering.
#
# Two services are supervised here, neither of which installs itself as a
# Windows service, so a reboot used to leave the model picker pointing at a dead
# port:
#
#   gateway  wb2api            127.0.0.1:7863  OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions
#   bridge   codex-chat-bridge 127.0.0.1:7864  Responses API -> chat/completions
#   anthropicBridge            127.0.0.1:7865  Anthropic Messages -> chat/completions
#
# One more thing is set up here: the `workbuddy` route in the model picker. That
# adapter is not reimplemented — it is mounted from `dsh-llm-workbuddy`, so a
# single install covers provider + gateway + bridge. When that plugin is also
# enabled standalone, whoever registers the route first keeps it and the other
# stands down, so both layouts are safe.
#
# The bridge is bundled with this plugin, so `bridge.command` stays empty and the
# shipped entry runs on the harness's own Node. Its upstream, bearer and
# conversation id are derived: upstream defaults to the gateway above, the bearer
# is read out of that gateway's `config.json`, and conversation id defaults to
# `auto` (required — the upstream answers 400 / code 11-128 without it and the
# gateway then disables the account).
#
# Paths support `~`, `$VAR` / `${VAR}` and Windows `%VAR%`, so this file can be
# copied between machines without rewriting the home directory.
#
# Set `autostart: false` to observe a service without the plugin ever spawning
# it — useful when something else (a scheduled task, a container) owns the
# process lifecycle.
- insert:
    - id: workbuddy-codex
      name: dsh-workbuddy-codex
      # No hard seam requirements: supervision is useful even where the tools
      # seam is absent, and the status tool attaches through `ctx.inject`.
      inject: []
      config:
        intervalMs: 15000
        probeTimeoutMs: 2000
        # Where the gateway keeps config.json; the bridge reads `api_key` from it.
        gatewayDir: ~/Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace/workbuddy2api-panel

        # The WorkBuddy route the model picker offers. Both empty fields below
        # inherit from the gateway entry, so the port and the api key are
        # configured exactly once.
        provider:
          enabled: true
          # Empty = follow gateway.baseURL.
          baseURL: ''
          # Empty = the gateway's config.json api_key (the same source the bridge uses).
          apiKey: ''
          discovery: true
          autoCheckin: true
          checkinAfterHour: 10

        gateway:
          enabled: true
          autostart: true
          baseURL: http://127.0.0.1:7863
          # The gateway answers 503 on /healthz while it is running but has no
          # usable upstream account; that is alive, not down.
          acceptStatus: [200, 503]
          command: ~/Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace/workbuddy2api-panel/wb2api.exe
          args: [-config, config.json]
          cwd: ~/Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace/workbuddy2api-panel

        bridge:
          enabled: true
          autostart: true
          baseURL: http://127.0.0.1:7864
          acceptStatus: [200]
          # Empty = run the bridge shipped in this package.
          command: ''
          # Empty = use the gateway's baseURL. Empty apiKey = read the gateway's config.json.
          upstream: ''
          apiKey: ''
          conversationId: auto
          # Models the bridge forwards. Empty = forward everything; the gateway
          # is what actually rejects a model your account tier cannot use.
          modelAllowlist: []
          # Tripwire, not a context manager. Above this estimated prompt size the
          # bridge answers 413 locally instead of spending an upstream account on
          # a request the upstream will reject with 400 prompt_too_long — a 400
          # that carries no `usage`, so the client cannot see how big it is, keeps
          # resending, and never compacts. Deliberately above the real 1048576
          # ceiling so an estimate that runs a little high cannot refuse a request
          # that would have fit. 0 disables it.
          maxPromptTokens: 1200000

        # Claude Desktop (3p mode) and Claude Code speak the Anthropic Messages
        # wire; the gateway speaks Chat Completions. This bridge translates, and
        # is derived exactly like the Responses bridge above (same upstream, same
        # bearer). Point Desktop's `inferenceGatewayBaseUrl` at it, and clear
        # `inferenceModels` so Desktop discovers the whole catalog instead.
        anthropicBridge:
          enabled: true
          autostart: true
          baseURL: http://127.0.0.1:7865
          acceptStatus: [200]
          # Empty = run the bridge shipped in this package.
          command: ''
          # Empty = use the gateway's baseURL. Empty apiKey = read the gateway's config.json.
          upstream: ''
          apiKey: ''
          # Used only when a client names a bare Claude alias (claude-sonnet-5-5,
          # opus). Empty = the first model in the gateway catalog.
          defaultModel: cn:deepseek-v4.1-flash

readme.text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

> **The repository is now `workbuddy2everything`. The npm package name stays `dsh-workbuddy-codex`.** GitHub redirects the old URL, so existing clones and `github:` dependencies keep working — nothing needs reinstalling.

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns a local WorkBuddy gateway into **a model backend for every client** — the model picker's provider, the gateway behind it, **and the two protocol bridges: Responses for OpenAI Codex CLI, Anthropic Messages for Claude Code and Claude Desktop**.

These have to line up before a WorkBuddy model can answer, and none of them installs itself as a Windows service:

| Port | Service | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `127.0.0.1:7863` | `wb2api` gateway | OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` |
| `127.0.0.1:7864` | Responses bridge (**bundled**) | Responses API → chat/completions, for Codex CLI |
| `127.0.0.1:7865` | Anthropic Messages bridge (**bundled**) | Anthropic `/v1/messages` → chat/completions, for Claude Code and Claude Desktop 3p |
| — | `workbuddy` provider | the model-picker route, **mounted from [`dsh-llm-workbuddy`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-llm-workbuddy)** |

These processes used to be started by hand, so a reboot silently left the model picker pointing at a dead port — the provider plugin loaded fine, listed models fine, and failed on the first request. This plugin supervises them: on load it probes each health endpoint, spawns whatever is missing, and re-checks on a timer so a crashed process comes back.

It deliberately **does not reimplement the gateway, and does not fork the adapter either**. The gateway is orchestrated as a process. The provider route is mounted by delegating to `dsh-llm-workbuddy` with `ctx.plugin()` — that package owns the ~2.5k-line WorkBuddy adapter, its settings section and its daily checkin scheduler, and a second copy of all that would drift the moment either side is updated. So one install covers provider + gateway + bridge.

The delegation is additive, not exclusive: if you also keep `dsh-llm-workbuddy` enabled standalone, whichever plugin registers the route first keeps it and the other stands down with a log line, so both layouts are safe.
Everything lives under the `workbuddy-codex` entry's `config` in the profile's `cordis.yml`; the shipped `cordis.patch.yml` has the full default set.

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gatewayDir` | `~/Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace/workbuddy2api-panel` | Where the gateway keeps `config.json`. The `api_key` in it is used for **both** the bridge and the provider, so the port and the key are configured once. |
| `provider.enabled` | `true` | Register the `workbuddy` route. |
| `provider.baseURL` | *(empty → `gateway.baseURL`)* | Gateway URL for the adapter. |
| `provider.discovery` | `true` | Ask the gateway's `/v1/models` for the live catalog. |
| `provider.autoCheckin` | `true` | Claim the daily WorkBuddy checkin. |
| `gateway.acceptStatus` | `[200, 503]` | The gateway answers `503` while running without a usable account — alive, not down. |
| `bridge.conversationId` | `auto` | Not optional against a WorkBuddy gateway: without it the upstream answers `400 / 11-128` and the gateway disables the account. |
| `bridge.maxPromptTokens` | `1200000` | Above this estimated prompt size the bridge answers `413` locally instead of forwarding a body the upstream rejects with `400 prompt_too_long`. `0` turns it off. See [Why a local prompt ceiling](#why-a-local-prompt-ceiling). |
| `anthropicBridge.enabled`
If `dsh-llm-workbuddy` is not installed at all, the plugin still supervises the gateway and the bridge and logs the one command that fixes it (`dsh plugin add dsh-llm-workbuddy`). Nothing throws.

`codex-cli` 0.1xx+ dropped `wire_api = "chat"` and speaks **only** the OpenAI Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`, SSE). A WorkBuddy gateway implements **only** Chat Completions (`POST /v1/chat/completions`). Point Codex straight at the gateway and every request dies with:

```
unexpected status 404 Not Found, url: http://127.0.0.1:7863/v1/responses
```

There is no config flag around this — Codex rejects `wire_api = "chat"` at load time. A translation layer is mandatory, so this package ships one:

```
Codex CLI --(Responses)--> bridge :7864 --(ChatCompletions)--> gateway :7863 --> WorkBuddy
```

It is the same code as [codex-chat-bridge](https://github.com/kangjiazhen/codex-chat-bridge), vendored at `bridge/codex-chat-bridge.mjs` (zero dependencies, runs on the harness's own Node) so installing this plugin is the only step — there is no second repo to clone and no path to fill in.

```bash
dsh plugin add git+https://github.com/kangjiazhen/workbuddy2everything.git
```

Or from a local checkout:

```bash
dsh plugin add file:/path/to/workbuddy2everything
```

The plugin ships a `cordis.patch.yml`, so the profile picks up the `workbuddy-codex` entry automatically once the package is a profile dependency.

The package itself has to stay installed — this plugin imports it to mount the provider, and there is no second copy of the adapter to drift. Leaving both in `bundles` is not harmful either: the first one to register keeps the route and the other logs `already-served`, but then this plugin is not the thing serving your models, which defeats the point.

`pnpm` rewrites `git+https://…` to `git+ssh://git@…` unless told otherwise, so an install on a machine without GitHub SSH keys fails with `Permission denied (publickey)`:

```bash
npm config set git-protocol https
```

Behind a proxy, git also needs to be told about it, because `pnpm` shells out to the `git` binary and does not forward its own proxy settings:

```bash
git config --global http.proxy http://127.0.0.1:7890
```

The bridge listens on `7864` and presents a Responses API. Point Codex at it:

```toml

model = "global:gpt-5.3-codex"
model_provider = "wb"

[model_providers.wb]
name = "workbuddy"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:7864/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
experimental_bearer_token = "anything"
request_max_retries = 2
stream_max_retries = 2
```

The bearer is not checked by the bridge — it authenticates to the gateway itself with the key it reads from the gateway's `config.json`. Set it to any non-empty string; Codex refuses to start without one.

Then just use Codex normally:bash
codex exec "list the files in this directory"
```

If you pick a model your account tier cannot use, the gateway answers `11158 model not allowed for user type [...]`. That is an account property, not a bridge fault — see [Model availability](#model-availability).

readme.section: Two settings you must not skip
readme.text: The WorkBuddy upstream validates three headers (`X-Conversation-ID`, `X-Conversation-Request-ID`, `X-Conversation-Message-ID`) and answers `400 {"code":"11-128","msg":"request illegal"}` when they are missing. The gateway classifies that as an *account fault* and responds by **disabling the account** — every account it touched, in the same pass. The resulting message says `re-login required`, which is misleading: the credentials are usually still valid and reviving them restores service immediately.

readme.section: Two settings you must not skip
readme.text:
So the bridge defaults to `conversationId: auto`: it derives a stable id per Codex session (from `prompt_cache_key`) and sends it as `metadata.conversation_id`. Do not blank this out. The plugin warns at startup if you do.

If you have already tripped it, revive the accounts rather than re-logging in:

```bash

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7863/panel/api/accounts/<uid>/revive
```

**2. The bearer must match the gateway's `api_key`.**

The gateway answers `401` to every request without it. Rather than making you copy the secret, the plugin reads `api_key` straight out of the gateway's `config.json` (that is what `gatewayDir` is for) and hands it to the bridge. Set `bridge.apiKey` only to override that.

readme.section: Images only arrive if the model catalog says so
readme.text:
Codex reads `~/.codex/models.json` *before* it builds a request. If the selected model's entry does not list `image` in `input_modalities`, Codex replaces every attachment with the literal string `image content omitted because you do not support image input` — the bridge never sees a picture, and the model falls back to reading the file with a shell tool or guessing.

So for every model the gateway reports as `supports_images: true`, the catalog entry has to say so:

readme.section: Images only arrive if the model catalog says so
Reasoning effort is a separate field on each side of the bridge
readme.text:
The two protocols name the same setting differently, and the name is the only thing they share:

| Side | Where the level lives |
| --- | --- |
| Responses (Codex) | `"reasoning": { "effort": "max" }` |
| Chat Completions (gateway) | `"reasoning_effort": "max"` |

readme.section: Reasoning effort is a separate field on each side of the bridge
readme.text: The bridge reads `reasoning.effort` and forwards it as the flat `reasoning_effort`, omitting the field when the client asked for no level so the upstream default still applies. Without that mapping every request reaches the backend at the gateway's default level, so `low` and `max` behave identically — the selector moves, the model does not think harder.

readme.section: Reasoning effort is a separate field on each side of the bridge
readme.text: Which levels exist is the gateway's call, not the bridge's. `reasoning_supported_efforts` in `GET /v1/models` is the authority; on this gateway 17 of 55 models offer `max`, and the rest answer with whatever subset they declare (some only `medium`, some `low`/`high`, some `high`/`xhigh`). A level the model does not declare is dropped by the gateway, silently. Pick the model first, then pick the level.

Claude Code and Claude Desktop (3p mode) speak the Anthropic Messages wire (`POST /v1/messages`, SSE). The gateway speaks only Chat Completions. A second bundled bridge translates between them, listening on `7865`.

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7865
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=anything      # the bridge does not check it; it authenticates upstream with the gateway's key
claude
```

Edit the config it actually reads (the UUID differs per install; `appliedId` in `_meta.json` names the live one):

```jsonc
// %LOCALAPPDATA%\Claude-3p\configLibrary\<appliedId>.json
{
  "inferenceGatewayBaseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:7865",
  "inferenceGatewayApiKey": "anything",

Three things matter:

- **Do not set `inferenceModels`.** Desktop treats that list as hand-written truth: while it is non-empty it skips `/v1/models` discovery and the picker shows only what you transcribed. Leave it out, turn `modelDiscoveryEnabled` on, and the picker becomes a live projection of the gateway catalog.
- **`inferenceGatewayBaseUrl` accepts `http://` on a loopback host**; any other host must be https.
- **`defaultModelEffort` only moves Desktop's "recommended" marker.** The level actually sent upstream is decided by the bridge (next section), so set both or neither — otherwise the picker and the wire disagree.

Every gateway model carries a `context_length`, `1000000` for most of them here. Desktop does **not** guess that number: it reads `max_input_tokens` off each `/v1/models` row and silently substitutes its own `200000` default when the field is absent. A bridge that drops the field therefore makes every model look like 200K — nothing to do with the gateway.

So the bridge publishes, per row:

| Discovery field | Source | What Desktop does with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_input_tokens` | gateway `context_length` / `max_allowed_size` | the window it displays; `>= 1000000` also counts as "1M" |
| `prefer_1m` | set when the same figure is `>= 1000000` | preselects the 1M variant instead of making the user pick it |
| `max_output_tokens` | gateway `max_output_tokens` | per-turn output ceiling |
| `max_effort_level` | top of the gateway's `reasoning_supported_efforts` | upper bound of the effort selector |
| `behaves_as` | fixed `claude-sonnet-5`, reasoning models only | borrows a Claude family's thinking UI; without it there is **no effort selector at all** |

`behaves_as` is the easy one to miss: Desktop renders an effort menu only for ids it can resolve to a built-in Claude family (`claude-<tier>-<version>`). A hashed id carries no family, so the bridge declares one explicitly. And the level that reaches the upstream does not depend on the client at all: when no `output_config.effort` arrives — which is the normal case, since Desktop only sends one after you touch the selector — the bridge picks the model's highest supported level. That is the only reliable place to make "think as hard as possible" the default.

readme.section: Why the model ids are rewritten as `claude-wb-…`
readme.text: Desktop runs every discovered row through a filter (`No()`): an id carrying another vendor's brand token (`kimi`, `gpt`, `deepseek`, `qwen`, `glm`, …) is dropped outright, and the id must also look like an Anthropic route (`claude…`). A real `cn:kimi-k3.1-pro` fails both — the picker comes up empty.

readme.section: Why the model ids are rewritten as `claude-wb-…`
readme.text: So the bridge hashes the real id into `claude-wb-<10 hex>` and publishes that, keeping the real id only in its in-memory catalog, while **the human-readable name rides in `display_name`** (`CN · Kimi-K3.1-Pro`). When a `claude-wb-…` comes back, the bridge maps it to the real id and forwards that.

readme.section: Why the model ids are rewritten as `claude-wb-…`
readme.text: One more trap: Desktop merges picker rows by `(name, Anthropic family)`. Several distinct gateway models share one display name (`cn:hy3` / `cn:hy3-x`, `cn:hy4-preview` / `cn:hy4-preview-f`, …), so copying the names verbatim **silently hides rows**. The bridge therefore appends the distinguishing tail of the id, but only where names actually collide: `CN · Hy3 (x)`, `Global · Auto (chat)`. Measured against this gateway: 52 models in, 52 rows in the picker.

readme.section: When a client names a bare Claude alias
readme.text: If a config you copied from elsewhere says `claude-sonnet-5-5` — an alias that never went through the picker, so the bridge has never seen it — the bridge answers from `anthropicBridge.defaultModel` instead of 404ing, falling back to the catalog head when that is empty. A translated config still produces text rather than leaving you to guess at a 404.

The defaults assume the usual layout and can be overridden in the profile's `cordis.yml`:

```yaml
- id: workbuddy-codex
  name: dsh-workbuddy-codex
  config:
    intervalMs: 15000        # re-probe cadence

Paths accept `~`, `$VAR` / `${VAR}`, and Windows `%VAR%`, so a config file can be copied between machines without rewriting the home directory.

`bridge.command` is empty on purpose. Setting it switches the plugin from "run the bundled bridge" to "supervise this command instead", which is how you'd point it at a different bridge build; `CCB_PORT`, `CCB_UPSTREAM` and the rest of the environment are still derived for you.

The gateway answers **`503`** on `/healthz` while it is running but has no usable upstream account yet (nothing signed in, or every account cooling down). That is *alive*, not *down*.

A supervisor that only accepted `2xx` would read that as "not started", spawn a second copy, and lose the port race. So the gateway entry accepts `[200, 503]` by default, while the bridge accepts `[200]` only.
Observe without ever spawning. Use this when something else owns the lifecycle — a scheduled task, a container, a wrapper script — and you only want the health reporting.

When the `tools` seam is mounted, the plugin registers `workbuddy_codex_status`:

```
gateway: up (http://127.0.0.1:7863/healthz, pid 14592)
bridge: up (http://127.0.0.1:7864/healthz)
anthropicBridge: up (http://127.0.0.1:7865/healthz, pid 14593)
```

Each line carries the live probe result, the supervised child pid, and the last spawn error if there was one — so "the model list is empty" can be told apart from "the port is dead" without reading logs.

If `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` is not importable, the tool is skipped with a warning rather than registered half-formed: `tools.register()` requires the `defineTool` shape (an `output { schema, render }` pair) and rejects anything else, so a raw descriptor would fail silently and the model would never see the tool. The supervisor and the provider run either way — neither depends on the tool.

- The first supervision pass runs asynchronously right after `apply()`, so a cold start never blocks the harness.
- The timer is `unref`'d — an idle supervisor cannot hold the process open.
- On dispose the timer stops and any child **this plugin spawned** is terminated. A service that was already running before the plugin loaded is left alone: it is probed and reported, never adopted, so unloading the plugin does not kill a process someone else started.

Which models answer is a property of your **WorkBuddy account tier**, not of this plugin or the bridge. A `personal_free_user` account, measured on 2026-10-21, could reach:

| Realm | Working |
| --- | --- |
| `global:` | `gpt-5.3-codex`, `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.2`, `kimi-k3`, `kimi-k2.6`, `hy4-preview`, `step-5-preview`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `minimax-m3.1-flash` |
| `cn:` | `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `glm-5.3` |

Every other GPT model (`gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.5`, the `gpt-6-*` family, …) answered `11158 model not allowed for user type [personal_free_user]`. That list moves with your subscription, so treat it as a snapshot, not a contract.

`modelAllowlist` exists to fail *fast* on models you know are unreachable: the bridge rejects them with a local `400 model_not_allowed` instead of letting the gateway classify the refusal as an account fault and disable the pool. Leaving it empty is the honest default.

An upstream `400 prompt_too_long` is not just a rejection — it returns **no `usage`**. A client that learns its own size from `usage` therefore cannot see how far over it is. It holds the last successful measurement, keeps resending the same oversized history, and never reaches the threshold that would trigger auto-compaction. Measured on a real session: the last success was `662,937` input tokens, the rejected body was `1,049,429`, and the client's counter stayed frozen at `662,937` — 70% of a 950k window — for the rest of the session. The overshoot was 849 tokens, and it was unrecoverable.

- **Images in tool results are re-attached, not serialized.** A Chat Completions `role: "tool"` message carries text only, so an image returned by a tool has nowhere to go. Stringifying it put the whole `data:` URL into the prompt as literal text; the upstream tokenizer then charged roughly one token per character. One 1080p screenshot (~570k base64 characters) was measured at 280k–594k input tokens — a single tool result could fill a 1M context. The bridge now keeps the text in the tool message, notes that images moved, and re-attaches them as real `image_url` parts on the next user message (after the whole run of tool results, so the assistant `tool_calls` pairing is not broken). Measured after the fix: the same 762,772-character screenshot costs **1,100** input tokens instead of 594,443, and the model reads the image normally. At most 8 images are hoisted per tool result; the rest are reported by count.
- **`maxPromptTokens` refuses locally.** Above the ceiling the bridge answers `413` with the estimated size and never contacts the upstream. No account is spent, no rate-limit cooldown is tripped, and the message says what to do.

Set it a little **above** the real ceiling (`1200000` for a `1048576`-token upstream) so an estimate that runs high cannot refuse a request that would have fit. The estimate is deliberately crude — ~4 chars/token for text, ~1 char/token for long base64 runs, a fixed vision cost per image — which is why it is a tripwire and not a context manager.

- Process supervision plus a request translator. It does not start, stop, or configure the *upstream* provider, and it has no opinion about which models your account may use.
- No restart backoff: a child that dies instantly is respawned once per `intervalMs`. If the binary is missing or the port is held by a foreign process, the logs will say so on every pass rather than spinning.
- `windowsHide: true` is set on spawn, so a supervised console child does not flash a window on Windows.
- Linux and macOS work with the same code; only the default paths in `cordis.patch.yml` are Windows-specific.
- The upstream WorkBuddy project has stopped maintenance and is actively tightening anti-proxy checks. This plugin keeps the chain alive; it cannot keep the upstream channel open.

- [codex-chat-bridge](https://github.com/kangjiazhen/codex-chat-bridge) — the bridge this plugin bundles, if you want it standalone.
- [LiteLLM](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm), [one-api](https://github.com/songquanpeng/one-api), [new-api](https://github.com/Calcium-Ion/new-api) — full gateways, if you need routing and key management rather than local process supervision.

[English](README.md) | **简体中文**

> **仓库已改名为 `workbuddy2everything`，npm 包名仍是 `dsh-workbuddy-codex`。** 旧地址有 301 跳转，已经 clone 的仓库和 `github:` 依赖都照常工作，不需要重装。

一个 DeepSeek Harness 插件，把本地 WorkBuddy 网关变成**任何客户端都能用的模型后端** —— 模型选择器的 provider、它背后的网关，**以及两条内置协议桥：给 OpenAI Codex CLI 的 Responses，给 Claude Code / Claude 桌面端的 Anthropic Messages**。

在 WorkBuddy 模型能回答之前，有这些环节必须同时对上，而它们都不会把自己装成 Windows 服务：

| 端口 | 服务 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `127.0.0.1:7863` | `wb2api` 网关 | OpenAI 兼容的 `/v1/chat/completions` |
| `127.0.0.1:7864` | Responses 桥（**内置**） | Responses API → chat/completions，供 Codex CLI 使用 |
| `127.0.0.1:7865` | Anthropic Messages 桥（**内置**） | Anthropic `/v1/messages` → chat/completions，供 Claude Code / Claude 桌面端 3p 使用 |
| — | `workbuddy` provider | 模型选择器里的那条路由，**从 [`dsh-llm-workbuddy`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-llm-workbuddy) 挂载而来** |

这些进程过去都要手动启动，于是重启一次电脑之后，模型选择器会悄无声息地指向一个死掉的端口 —— provider 插件加载正常、模型列表正常，直到第一次请求才失败。本插件接管它们：加载时探测各自的健康端点，缺什么就拉起什么，并按定时器复查，进程崩了会自动回来。

它刻意**既不重写网关，也不 fork 适配器**。网关只做进程编排；provider 路由则是用 `ctx.plugin()` 委派给 `dsh-llm-workbuddy` 挂载出来的 —— 那个包自己拥有约 2500 行的 WorkBuddy 适配器、设置面板和每日签到调度器，再抄一份只会让两边一更新就分叉。所以装一次就同时得到 provider + 网关 + 桥。

这种委派是叠加式的，不是排他的：如果你同时保留独立的 `dsh-llm-workbuddy`，谁先注册这条路由谁就拥有它，另一个会在日志里说明后退让，两种装法都安全。
全部位于 profile 的 `cordis.yml` 中 `workbuddy-codex` 条目的 `config` 下；随包发布的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里是完整的默认值。

| 键 | 默认值 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gatewayDir` | `~/Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace/workbuddy2api-panel` | 网关存放 `config.json` 的目录。其中的 `api_key` 会同时用于**桥和 provider**，所以端口与密钥只需配一次。 |
| `provider.enabled` | `true` | 是否注册 `workbuddy` 路由。 |
| `provider.baseURL` | *(留空 → 用 `gateway.baseURL`)* | 适配器要访问的网关地址。 |
| `provider.discovery` | `true` | 向网关的 `/v1/models` 拉取实时模型目录。 |
| `provider.autoCheckin` | `true` | 领取 WorkBuddy 每日签到。 |
| `gateway.acceptStatus` | `[200, 503]` | 网关在无可用账号时仍会跑着并返回 `503`，那是活着，不是挂了。 |
| `bridge.conversationId` | `auto` | 对着 WorkBuddy 网关不是可选项：缺了它上游会回 `400 / 11-128`，网关随即停用该账号。 |
| `bridge.maxPromptTokens` | `1200000` | 估算提示词超过它就由桥在本地回 `413`，不把一个注定被上游以 `400 prompt_too_long` 拒绝的请求转发出去。`0` 关闭。见[为什么要在本地设上限](#为什么要在本地设上限)。 |
| `anthropicBridge.enabled` | `true` | 是否监护 Anthropic Messages 桥。 |
| `anthropicBridge.baseURL` | `http://127.0.0.1:7865` | 桥监听地址，也就是 Claude 那边要填的 gateway base URL。 |
| `anthropicBridge.upstream` | *(留空 → 用 `gateway.baseURL`)* | 桥转发的上游。留空即复用同一条网关。 |
| `anthropicBridge.apiKey` | *(留空 → 读网关注入的 `api_key`)* | 上游 bearer。留空时与 Responses 桥共用同一份密钥，不会有两份会漂移的秘密。 |
| `anthropicBridge.defaultModel` | *(留空 → 目录第一条)* | 只在客户端直接点名一个裸 Claude 别名（`claude-so
如果根本没装 `dsh-llm-workbuddy`，插件照旧监护网关与桥，并打印出补装它的那一条命令（`dsh plugin add dsh-llm-workbuddy`）。任何情况下都不会抛错。

`codex-cli` 0.1xx 之后删掉了 `wire_api = "chat"`，只讲 OpenAI 的 **Responses** 协议（`POST /v1/responses`，SSE）。而 WorkBuddy 网关只实现 **Chat Completions**（`POST /v1/chat/completions`）。让 Codex 直连网关，每个请求都会死在这里：

```
unexpected status 404 Not Found, url: http://127.0.0.1:7863/v1/responses
```

这不是配置项能绕过的问题 —— Codex 在加载阶段就直接拒绝 `wire_api = "chat"`。转换层是必需品，所以本包自带一个：

```
Codex CLI --(Responses)--> 桥 :7864 --(ChatCompletions)--> 网关 :7863 --> WorkBuddy
```
它和 [codex-chat-bridge](https://github.com/kangjiazhen/codex-chat-bridge) 是同一份代码，以 `bridge/codex-chat-bridge.mjs` 内置（零依赖，跑在 Harness 自带的 Node 上），所以装这一个插件就够了 —— 不需要再 clone 第二个仓库，也没有任何路径要你填。

```bash
dsh plugin add git+https://github.com/kangjiazhen/workbuddy2everything.git
```

或者从本地检出安装：

```bash
dsh plugin add file:/path/to/workbuddy2everything
```

插件自带 `cordis.patch.yml`，所以只要它成为 profile 依赖，profile 就会自动拿到 `workbuddy-codex` 这一条。

除非另有指定，`pnpm` 会把 `git+https://…` 改写成 `git+ssh://git@…`，因此在没有配置 GitHub SSH 密钥的机器上，安装会失败并报 `Permission denied (publickey)`：

```bash
npm config set git-protocol https
```

如果走代理，还得单独告诉 git —— `pnpm` 是通过调用 git 二进制实现的，不会把自己的代理设置传下去：

```bash
git config --global http.proxy http://127.0.0.1:7890
```

桥监听 `7864`，对外提供 Responses API。把 Codex 指过去：

```toml

model = "global:gpt-5.3-codex"
model_provider = "wb"

[model_providers.wb]
name = "workbuddy"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:7864/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
experimental_bearer_token = "anything"
request_max_retries = 2
stream_max_retries = 2
```

桥本身不校验这个 bearer —— 它用自己的方式（从网关 `config.json` 读出的 key）向上游认证。填任意非空字符串即可，因为 Codex 没有它就不启动。

之后正常用 Codex 就行：bash
codex exec "列出当前目录的文件"
```

如果选到了你的账号档位用不了的模型，网关会返回 `11158 model not allowed for user type [...]`。那是账号属性，不是桥的故障 —— 见[模型可用性](#模型可用性)。

readme.section: 两个绝对不能跳过的设置
readme.text:
**1. `conversation_id` —— 能把账号搞封的那个。**

WorkBuddy 上游会校验三个头（`X-Conversation-ID`、`X-Conversation-Request-ID`、`X-Conversation-Message-ID`），缺任意一个就返回 `400 {"code":"11-128","msg":"request illegal"}`。网关把这种情况归类为*账号故障*，处理方式是**禁用账号** —— 而且是一轮里把碰到的账号全部禁用。它给出的原因是 `re-login required`，这句话有误导性：凭证通常仍然有效，解冻就能立刻恢复服务。

所以桥默认 `conversationId: auto`：按 Codex 会话（取自 `prompt_cache_key`）推导出一个稳定 id，作为 `metadata.conversation_id` 发送。不要把它置空，插件会在启动时告警。

如果不幸已经踩了，解冻账号即可，不需要重新登录：

```bash

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7863/panel/api/accounts/<uid>/revive
```

**2. bearer 必须和网关的 `api_key` 一致。**

没有它，网关对每个请求都回 `401`。为了不让你手工抄密钥，插件直接从网关的 `config.json` 里读 `api_key`（`gatewayDir` 就是干这个的）并交给桥。只有要覆盖时才设 `bridge.apiKey`。

readme.section: 图片能不能进去，取决于模型目录
readme.text:
Codex 在**拼请求之前**会先读 `~/.codex/models.json`。如果所选模型的条目里 `input_modalities` 没有 `image`，Codex 自己就会把附件替换成一句 `image content omitted because you do not support image input` —— 桥根本收不到图，模型只能去读文件或者瞎猜。

所以凡是网关报 `supports_images: true` 的模型，条目里必须写上：

```json
{
  "slug": "cn:deepseek-v4.1-flash",
  "input_modalities": ["text", "image"]
}

桥对 `input_image` 是原样透传的（转成 `{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:..."}}`），所以 Codex 侧图被吞掉，唯一原因就是目录条目不认图。以 `GET /v1/models` 返回的 `supports_images` 为准。

readme.section: 推理档位在两种协议里是两个字段
readme.text:
同一件事，两边名字不同，而且只有名字不同：

| 一侧 | 档位放在哪 |
| --- | --- |
| Responses（Codex） | `"reasoning": { "effort": "max" }` |
| Chat Completions（网关） | `"reasoning_effort": "max"` |

桥读 `reasoning.effort`，转发成扁平的 `reasoning_effort`；客户端没指定档位时不写这个字段，让上游默认值生效。少了这层映射，所有请求都会按网关默认档跑，`low` 和 `max` 行为完全一样 —— 选择器动了，模型没多想一步。

档位有哪些由网关说了算，不由桥决定。`GET /v1/models` 里的 `reasoning_supported_efforts` 才是权威：本网关 55 个模型里 17 个支持 `max`，其余按各自声明的子集走（有的只有 `medium`，有的 `low`/`high`，有的 `high`/`xhigh`）。模型没声明的档位会被网关静默丢弃。先选模型，再选档位。
Claude Code 和 Claude 桌面端（3p 模式）说的是 Anthropic Messages 协议（`POST /v1/messages`，SSE），网关只说 Chat Completions。第二条内置桥把前者翻成后者，监听 `7865`。

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7865
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=anything      # 桥不校验；它用网关的 key 向上游认证
claude
```

改它自己那份生效配置（每个安装的 UUID 不同，`_meta.json` 里的 `appliedId` 指向当前生效的那份）：

```jsonc
// %LOCALAPPDATA%\Claude-3p\configLibrary\<appliedId>.json
{
  "inferenceGatewayBaseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:7865",
  "inferenceGatewayApiKey": "anything",

三个要点：

- **不要写 `inferenceModels`。** 桌面端的 `inferenceModels` 是「手写死」的清单，一旦非空就会绕过 `/v1/models` 发现，下拉框只剩你抄进去的那几条。留空并打开 `modelDiscoveryEnabled`，下拉框才是网关目录的实时投影。
- **`inferenceGatewayBaseUrl` 允许 `http://` 回环地址**，其他主机名必须是 https。
- **`defaultModelEffort` 只影响桌面端「推荐」标记**，真正发给上游的档位由桥决定（见下节）。所以两处都不留白，行为才可预期。

readme.section: 上下文窗口与思考档位
readme.text:
网关目录里每个模型都有 `context_length`，本网关多数是 `1000000`。桌面端**不会**自己猜这个数：它读 `/v1/models` 每行的 `max_input_tokens`，缺失就套用自己的默认值 `200000`。桥不把这个字段透出去，下拉框里的模型就一律显示 200K，跟网关无关。

桥因此每行都带上：

readme.section: 上下文窗口与思考档位
readme.text:
| 发现行字段 | 来源 | 桌面端拿它做什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_input_tokens` | 网关 `context_length` / `max_allowed_size` | 显示的上下文窗口；`>= 1000000` 时认作「1M 模型」 |
| `prefer_1m` | 同上 `>= 1000000` 时置 `true` | 自动选中 1M 变体，而不是让用户手点 |
| `max_output_tokens` | 网关 `max_output_tokens` | 单轮输出上限 |
| `max_effort_level` | 网关 `reasoning_supported_efforts` 的最高档 | 思考档位选择器的上限 |
| `behaves_as` | 桥固定填 `claude-sonnet-5`（仅推理模型） | 套用 Claude 家族的思考 UI，否则**没有档位选择器** |

readme.section: 上下文窗口与思考档位
readme.text: `behaves_as` 是最容易漏的一条：桌面端只给它认识的 Claude 家族（`claude-<tier>-<version>`）渲染思考档位菜单。合成 id 里没有家族信息，所以桥单独声明一个。同时**下发档位不依赖客户端**：客户端没写 `output_config.effort` 时（桌面端在你动过选择器之前就是不发），桥取该模型支持的最高档。想要「默认最努力」，桥这一层是唯一可靠的地方。

readme.section: 为什么模型 id 要改写成 `claude-wb-…`
readme.text:
桌面端对发现回来的每一行都跑一个过滤器（`No()`）：id 里带别家品牌字样的（`kimi`、`gpt`、`deepseek`、`qwen`、`glm`…）直接丢弃，而且它还要 id 长得像 Anthropic 的路由（`claude…`）。真实的 `cn:kimi-k3.1-pro` 两条都过不了 —— 下拉框会空。

所以桥把真实 id 哈希成 `claude-wb-<10 hex>` 再发出去，真实 id 只存在于桥的内存目录里，而**人能读的名字走 `display_name`**（`CN · Kimi-K3.1-Pro`）。桥收到 `claude-wb-…` 再翻回真实 id 转发给网关。

readme.section: 为什么模型 id 要改写成 `claude-wb-…`
readme.text: 还有一个坑：桌面端会按 `(name, Anthropic 家族)` 合并下拉框行。网关有几组不同的模型共用同一个显示名（`cn:hy3` / `cn:hy3-x`，`cn:hy4-preview` / `cn:hy4-preview-f` 等），直接照抄就会**静默少几条**。桥因此只在名字撞车时给标签补上 id 尾部做区分：`CN · Hy3 (x)`、`Global · Auto (chat)`。本网关实测 52 个模型 → 下拉框 52 条。

readme.section: 客户端直接点名裸 Claude 别名时
readme.text: 如果你写的配置里模型名是 `claude-sonnet-5-5` 这种裸别名（它没经过下拉框，所以桥不认识），桥不会 404，而是回落到 `anthropicBridge.defaultModel`，该值留空则用目录第一条。这样一个「从别处抄来的配置」也能出字，而不是让用户对着一条 404 猜。

默认值假设了常规目录结构，可在 profile 的 `cordis.yml` 中覆盖：

```yaml
- id: workbuddy-codex
  name: dsh-workbuddy-codex
  config:
    intervalMs: 15000        # 复查间隔

路径支持 `~`、`$VAR` / `${VAR}` 以及 Windows 的 `%VAR%`，所以同一份配置可以在机器之间直接拷。

`bridge.command` 留空是刻意的。一旦填了，插件就从「运行内置桥」切换成「监管这条命令」，用于指向另一个桥构建；`CCB_PORT`、`CCB_UPSTREAM` 等环境变量依然由插件推导。

网关在**进程活着但上游账号暂时不可用**时（没登录，或所有账号都在冷却），`/healthz` 返回 **`503`**。那是*活着*，不是*挂了*。

只认 `2xx` 的监管器会把它读成「没启动」，于是拉起第二份、抢端口失败。所以网关那条默认接受 `[200, 503]`，而桥只接受 `[200]`。
只观察、永不拉起。当生命周期由别的东西掌管时用这个 —— 计划任务、容器、包装脚本 —— 你只想拿到健康状态上报。

当 `tools` 缝挂载后，插件会注册 `workbuddy_codex_status`：

```
gateway: up (http://127.0.0.1:7863/healthz, pid 14592)
bridge: up (http://127.0.0.1:7864/healthz)
anthropicBridge: up (http://127.0.0.1:7865/healthz, pid 14593)
```

每行都带实时探测结果、被监管子进程的 pid，以及最近一次拉起失败的错误 —— 这样「模型列表是空的」和「端口死了」不用翻日志也能分清。

如果 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 无法导入，工具会记一条警告然后跳过，而不是用原始描述符硬塞：`tools.register()` 只接受 `defineTool` 造出来的形状（必须带 `output { schema, render }`），塞原始描述符会被静默拒绝，模型永远看不到这个工具。监管与 provider 不受影响 —— 它们都不依赖这个工具。

- 第一次监管在 `apply()` 之后异步立刻执行，冷启动不会阻塞 Harness。
- 定时器是 `unref` 过的 —— 空转的监管器不会把进程吊住。
- dispose 时停掉定时器，并终止**本插件自己拉起**的子进程。加载插件之前就在跑的服务只探测上报、绝不接管，所以卸载插件不会杀掉别人启动的进程。

哪些模型能应答，取决于你的 **WorkBuddy 账号档位**，与本插件和桥无关。一个 `personal_free_user` 账号在 2026-10-21 实测能触达：

| 域 | 可用 |
| --- | --- |
| `global:` | `gpt-5.3-codex`、`glm-5.3`、`glm-5.2`、`kimi-k3`、`kimi-k2.6`、`hy4-preview`、`step-5-preview`、`deepseek-v4.1-flash`、`minimax-m3.1-flash` |
| `cn:` | `deepseek-v4.1-flash`、`deepseek-v4-pro`、`glm-5.3` |

其余 GPT 模型（`gpt-5.4`、`gpt-5.5`、`gpt-6-*` 全系……）一律返回 `11158 model not allowed for user type [personal_free_user]`。这份名单随你的订阅变动，请当作快照而非承诺。
`modelAllowlist` 的用途是让已知不可达的模型**快速失败**：桥直接本地回 `400 model_not_allowed`，而不是让网关把拒绝归类成账号故障、进而禁用整个池子。留空是诚实的默认。

readme.section: 为什么要在本地设上限
readme.text:
上游的 `400 prompt_too_long` 不只是拒绝 —— 它**不返回 `usage`**。靠 `usage` 得知自己大小的客户端因此看不到超了多少，只能拿最后一次成功的数字反复重发同一份历史，永远到不了触发自动压缩的阈值。实测一个真实会话：最后一次成功是 `662,937` 输入 token，被拒的请求体是 `1,049,429`，而客户端计数器整个会话冻结在 `662,937`（950k 窗口的 70%）。超出量只有 849 个 token，却完全无法恢复。

两件事桥直接处理了：

readme.section: 为什么要在本地设上限
readme.text:
- **工具结果里的图片是搬运，不是序列化。** Chat Completions 的 `role: "tool"` 消息只能装文本，工具返回的图片无处可放；把它 `JSON.stringify` 会把整个 `data:` URL 变成字面文本，上游分词器按约 1 token/字符计费。一张 1080p 截图（约 570k 个 base64 字符）实测 280k–594k 输入 token，一个工具结果就能填满 1M 上下文。现在桥把文本留在工具消息里、注明图片已移动，并在下一条 user 消息上（放在整批工具结果之后，以免破坏 assistant `tool_calls` 的配对）作为真正的 `image_url` part 重新挂上。修复后同一张 762,772 字符的截图只花 **1,100** 输入 token，模型也能正常读到图。单次最多搬运 8 张，其余按数量报告。
- **`maxPromptTokens` 在本地就拒绝。** 超过上限时桥直接回 `413` 并给出估算值，完全不接触上游：不消耗账号、不触发限流冷却，报错里写清楚了该怎么做。

readme.section: 为什么要在本地设上限
readme.text:
把它设在真实上限**之上**一点（`1048576` 的上游用 `1200000`），估算偏高时才不会误伤本来能过的请求。估算刻意做得很粗 —— 文本约 4 字符/token、长 base64 约 1 字符/token、每张图一个固定视觉开销 —— 所以它是保险丝，不是上下文管理器。

这个默认值放在桥**自己的代码里**，而不是某个启动器的环境变量里：桥会被 DSH supervisor 拉起、被 `start-bridge.vbs` 拉起、调试时还会手工 `node bridge.mjs`，只有把默认值写进代码，换一条启动路径才不会静默失去保护。

- 只做进程监管加请求翻译。它不启动、停止或配置*上游* provider，也不对你账号能用哪些模型发表意见。
- 没有重启退避：瞬间死掉的子进程每个 `intervalMs` 会被拉起一次。如果二进制缺失或端口被别人占着，日志每轮都会说明，不会空转。
- spawn 时设了 `windowsHide: true`，被监管的控制台子进程不会在 Windows 上闪窗。
- Linux 和 macOS 用同一份代码即可；只有 `cordis.patch.yml` 里的默认路径是 Windows 专用的。
- 上游 WorkBuddy 项目已停止维护，并正在收紧反代检测。本插件能让链路活着，但保不住上游通道本身。

- [codex-chat-bridge](https://github.com/kangjiazhen/codex-chat-bridge) —— 本插件内置的那座桥，想单独用可以去这里。
- [LiteLLM](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm)、[one-api](https://github.com/songquanpeng/one-api)、[new-api](https://github.com/Calcium-Ion/new-api) —— 完整网关，如果你需要路由与密钥管理，而不是本地进程监管。
